```bash
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter sonarqube   # SonarQube integration
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter automake    # Automake integration

# Multiple reporters simultaneously (if supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console --reporter junit::out=results.xml
```

### Test Output Control
The custom `VerboseConsoleReporter` provides enhanced output:
- Test case start/end notifications with timing
- Section execution tracking
- Color-coded success/failure indicators
- Duration reporting for performance analysis

## Test Data Management

### Using TEST_DATA_DIR
All test data is accessible via the `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition:

```cpp
std::string mesh_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/20mm_cube.obj";
std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/printer.ini";
```

### Available Test Assets

#### 3D Models
- **Basic shapes**: `20mm_cube.obj`, `pyramid.obj`, `sphere.obj`
- **Complex geometry**: `extruder_idler.obj`, `ipadstand.obj`, `bridge.obj`
- **Edge cases**: `cube_with_hole.obj`, `sloping_hole.obj`, `small_dorito.obj`

#### File Format Tests
- **STL variants**: ASCII/binary, different line endings, Unicode names
- **3MF files**: Multi-material, complex assemblies
- **Configuration files**: Various printer/material profiles

#### Test Utilities
The `Test` namespace provides helper functions:
```cpp
using namespace Slic3r::Test;

// Load standard test meshes
TriangleMesh mesh = mesh(TestMesh::cube_20x20x20);

// Standard test configurations
DynamicPrintConfig config = config(TestConfig::PLA_default);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

This comprehensive guide ensures robust, maintainable, and efficient testing practices for OrcaSlicer development with Claude Code, incorporating all critical knowledge from the official Catch2 documentation.
</system-reminder>

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Record the numbers the tool-loading decision will rest on

The catalog grows from five tools to about thirty-seven over this journey, and
the decision to defer loading is supposed to be made on measurements rather
than on the whiteboard. Three of them were missing.

Cached input tokens: the provider reports how much of an input it served from
its prompt cache, and that is the number that says whether keeping the tools
array byte-identical across a chat is working. The usage listener now carries
a small record instead of three loose counters, reads
usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens, and the live harness logs it on
every request, including when it is zero -- a chat that stops caching should
be visible as a number, not as silence.

Definition bytes per adapter: one test per adapter prints the count and the
serialized size and fails only on runaway growth. The bounds are an alarm, not
a target. Today: in-app 7 definitions, 3,145 bytes; MCP 5 definitions, 3,147
bytes.

The guide also now says plainly that dropping outputSchema saved MCP bytes and
not in-app ones -- the in-app adapter has only ever sent input_schema as
parameters, so no in-app turn was carrying them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -7

lines: Tool count is bounded by what a turn loads, not by what the app can do. The evidence behind these rules: OpenAI's function-calling guidance keeps fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn and defers the rest; Anthropic's [tool-writing guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) asks for a few tools targeting high-impact workflows and names "tools that merely wrap existing software functionality or API endpoints" as the common error; a [domain-oriented MCP study](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22063v1) measured a generic thin-tool interface below raw SQL and domain-shaped tools far above both; and the "god tool" that dispatches many unrelated actions through one `action` parameter is a documented anti-pattern. The current five-tool MCP catalog measures about 1.9 KB per definition, two thirds of it output schema.

- **Loading, for now.** Every registered tool loads on every turn in both adapters: the in-app adapter sends the full function list with each request, and MCP `tools/list` returns the whole catalog. This is the simplest correct behaviour and it keeps the tools array byte-identical across a chat, which is what OpenAI's prompt cache keys on. The budget of 20 definitions per turn is a measured trigger, not a gate: the live regression records definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens per request, and the journey catalog below will exceed 20 definitions from its first milestone. That is accepted until those measurements show selection errors or context pressure.

+- **The M0 baseline, measured on Windows against the live app.** In-app: 7 definitions, 3,145 bytes. MCP: 5 definitions, 3,147 bytes. Across twenty live requests in the `--live-agent` regression, input ran 803 to 3,889 tokens; the first request of a conversation cached nothing and later requests in the same conversation cached 77 to 86 per cent of their input (3,889 in, 3,328 cached). That is the prompt cache doing its job on a byte-identical tools array, and it is the figure a later catalog must be compared against: the cost of a definition is what it adds to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn.

- **Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Use the platform's own deferral, never a hand-rolled switcher. On the in-app side that is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API, documented for `gpt-5.4` and later; support on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unverified. On the MCP side clients defer on their own, as Claude Code does. Toolsets are the deferral unit, and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. An enable-toolset tool that rewrites the tools array breaks the prompt cache on every switch and is not to be built.

- **Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing a slicer user would name: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Not a wrapper per Orca function, and not an interpreter for a list of unrelated commands. Optional facets of one operation are fine when each is independently typed and conflicting facets are rejected.

- **Batch only where items share a shape.** A list of setting changes, a list of intent fields, a list of annotations, a list of per-object layout rows. A list that mixes transforms, imports, and deletes is the god tool and is refused.

content.text: Four questions, all of them things that change what I build. After these I'll run straight through M1 and onward without checking in.

questions.question: When the agent writes down the print intent or its own plan, should that count as a change to the project — the same way moving an object or editing a setting does?

options.label: No, just announce it
options.description: The panel refreshes, but the project revision does not move. Nothing pending gets cancelled. This is what I recommend: settings_apply_patch demands an exact revision match, so if recording a plan bumped the revision, the agent would cancel its own pending settings change just by writing down what it intends to do.
options.preview:
plan_set -> panel refreshes, revision unchanged
settings_apply_patch (pending) -> still valid

options.label: Yes, a real change
options.description: Intent and plan writes bump the revision and cancel anything waiting for approval, exactly as the handoff says. Honest and simple, but the agent must never write a plan while one of its own changes is waiting for you.

options.label: Split it
options.description: Region marks count as real changes (they generate supports, paint, modifiers in the model). Intent and plan only announce themselves. More code, but each kind gets the truthful answer.

questions.question: Should the agent be able to change print speeds in M4, or only the support, adhesion, seam, wall, infill and shell settings the handoff lists?

options.label: Start without, add if needed
options.description: Build the handoff's list, then run the eval. If the agent cannot hit 'under five hours' without speed, that is the evidence for adding speed keys, and I add them in the same milestone. Recommended: every new key costs a full audit of Orca's normalizer, so I would rather pay for the ones the eval proves are needed.

options.label: Include speed now
options.description: Add the speed family up front. Time budget is one of the things people actually ask for, so the agent will reach for it. Costs more audit work in M4 and makes the milestone longer.

options.label: Never speed
options.description: Keep speed a human decision. The agent trades time through layer height, infill and supports only.

questions.question: The tools that return pictures — reading an image you attached, and rendering the plate so the agent can look at it. Both need image plumbing in two adapters first. Ship them in M6, or leave them out of this journey?

options.description: The agent can look at a reference photo or drawing you attached, which is how people actually explain what they want. Rendering the plate waits. Recommended: half the work, most of the value, and the export journey does not need the agent to see the plate.

options.label: Both in M6
options.description: Agent can also render the prepared plate and look at it before slicing. Useful for catching an obviously wrong orientation, but it is the more expensive half and the agent already gets geometry facts as numbers.

options.label: Neither for now
options.description: Finish the model-file-to-G-code journey with no pictures at all, and revisit once it works end to end.

input.old_string: Node is required: the Agent and Home pages are built from TypeScript and their `index.html` is generated, not committed, so a tree without npm fails at configure time and an app built without them shows no Agent panel at all. The Python bridge tests need a `python3` that machine may not have; say so rather than reporting them run.
input.new_string:
Node is required: the Agent and Home pages are built from TypeScript and their `index.html` is generated, not committed, so a tree without npm fails at configure time and an app built without them shows no Agent panel at all.

The Python bridge tests run there too, with the helper named explicitly, since the default path in `tests/mcp/test_bridge_process.py` is the macOS bundle:

```sh
JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=build/src/Release/jusprin-mcp.exe python -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp
```

As of 2026-09-16 that reports 8 failures on Windows, all in the live-peer paths — SSE progress, client cancellation, EOF with a pending call, stdout backpressure, the live catalog's header mirroring, and a malformed peer result. They are not caused by any JusPrin change: building the helper from the previous commit reproduces the same 8. The suite had only ever been run on macOS and Linux, so treat them as an unexamined platform gap and do not read a green Windows run into a PR that has not had one.

input.title: Fix the 8 Windows MCP bridge test failures
input.tldr:
While verifying M0 I ran the Python bridge tests on Windows for the first time. Eight of them fail in the live-peer paths, and building the helper from an older commit reproduces the same eight, so it is a platform gap nobody has looked at. A separate session could work out whether the helper misbehaves on Windows or the tests assume POSIX.</tldr>
<parameter name="prompt">In C:\src\JusPrin (branch claude/journey-tools-m0 or later), the Python MCP bridge tests fail on Windows in eight live-peer cases. Investigate and fix whichever side is wrong.

Run them with:
  $env:JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE = "C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe"
  C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp

Failing as of 2026-09-16:
- test_client_cancellation_and_eof_close_http (both modern=False and True) - KeyError 'method': expected a notifications/progress frame, got something else
- test_progress_and_terminal_sse
- test_cancellation_discards_progress_queued_behind_backpressure
- test_eof_with_pending_call
- test_live_catalog_header_mirroring_and_version_warning
- test_malformed_peer_result_becomes_an_error_not_invalid_stdout
- test_one_process_follows_app_start_stop_and_replacement ('workspace_unavailable' != 'connection_lost')

These are NOT regressions: building jusprin-mcp from commit f797b2cd62 (before the M0 work) reproduces the same eight. The suite had only ever been run on macOS and Linux (see tests/mcp/linux/run.sh and the verification section of agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md).

The question to answer: does the stdio bridge (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/) genuinely behave differently on Windows - non-blocking stdio, select() on pipes, SSE framing, process teardown - or do the tests assume POSIX semantics the helper is right to not provide? Fix the side that is wrong, keep the macOS/Linux runs green, and record the finding in the guide's verification section, which currently documents the failures as an unexamined platform gap.

## 1. Plater's slicing entry points

### `Plater::reslice()` — `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16010`
```cpp
void Plater::reslice()
```
No arguments, no plate argument. **It always slices `p->partplate_list.get_curr_plate()`** — plate selection is an implicit precondition, established by the caller.

Order of operations:
- `Plater.cpp:16014` — early-return if `p->process_completed_with_error == p->partplate_list.get_curr_plate_index()` ("invalid data" state), after `reset_gcode_toolpaths()`. **Silent no-op; the caller gets no return value at all (`void`).**
- `Plater.cpp:16023` — early-return if the SLA gizmo is in editing mode. `is_in_editing_mode(true)` with `true` **shows a notification** to the user.
- `Plater.cpp:16027-16033` — `stop_queue(this->get_ui_job_worker(), 10000)`; returns silently if UI jobs will not stop within 10 s.
- `Plater.cpp:16046` — `unsigned int state = this->p->update_background_process(true);` (force_validation = true).
- `Plater.cpp:16050` — `this->p->background_process.set_task(PrintBase::TaskParams());`
- `Plater.cpp:16053` — `bool result = this->p->restart_background_process(state | priv::UPDATE_BACKGROUND_PROCESS_FORCE_RESTART);`
- `Plater.cpp:16056-16062` — if `state & UPDATE_BACKGROUND_PROCESS_INVALID`, logs, calls `update_fff_scene_only_shells()`, returns. The error was already surfaced as a notification inside `update_background_process` (see §1c).
- `Plater.cpp:16066-16078` — slice-all continuation hack: if `!result && p->m_slice_all && m_cur_slice_plate < plate_count-1`, it **fabricates** `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, 0, Finished, nullptr)` and queues it so `on_process_completed` advances to the next plate. Sets `p->m_is_slicing = true`.
- `Plater.cpp:16080-16082` — `if (result) p->m_is_slicing = true;`
- `Plater.cpp:16086-16110` — three-way branch on `background_process.running()` / `!empty() && !idle()` / else. In the *else* (idle) branch it uses the **previous** result and calls `current_plate->update_slice_result_valid_state(true|false)` based on `has_printable_instances()`. So `reslice()` returning without actually slicing still marks the plate valid.
- `Plater.cpp:16118` — `p->preview->reload_print();`
- `Plater.cpp:16122` — `record_slice_preset("slicing")`.

**`reslice()` never switches to Preview.** That is done by the callers.

### `on_action_slice_plate` — `Plater.cpp:10173`
```cpp
void Plater::priv::on_action_slice_plate(SimpleEvent&)
```
Bound at `Plater.cpp:5302`: `q->Bind(EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE, &priv::on_action_slice_plate, this);`
Body: `Model::setExtruderParams` / `Model::setPrintSpeedTable`, then `m_slice_all = false; q->reslice();` then `if (q->auto_preview_after_slice()) q->select_view_3D("Preview");` (`Plater.cpp:10186-10187`).

`auto_preview_after_slice()` / `set_auto_preview_after_slice()` are **fork-added** (`Plater.hpp:335-336`, member `m_auto_preview_after_slice` at `Plater.hpp:976`); `ShellController.cpp:255` sets it false and restores it at `ShellController.cpp:415`.

### `on_action_slice_all` — `Plater.cpp:10193` (this is "slice all"; there is no `Plater::reslice_all()`)
```cpp
void Plater::priv::on_action_slice_all(SimpleEvent&)
```
Bound at `Plater.cpp:5303`. It sets the slice-all state itself:
```cpp
m_slice_all = true;
m_slice_all_only_has_gcode = true;
m_cur_slice_plate = 0;
//select plate
q->select_plate(m_cur_slice_plate);
q->reslice();
if (!m_is_publishing && q->auto_preview_after_slice())
    q->select_view_3D("Preview");
```
(`Plater.cpp:10205-10212`). Plus `preview->get_canvas3d()->_update_select_plate_toolbar_stats_item(true)` at `Plater.cpp:10216-10217`, guarded by `auto_preview_after_slice()` (fork-added guard, per its comment).

The plate-to-plate advance during slice-all is **not** a loop: it is driven from `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10096-10107`:
```cpp
m_cur_slice_plate++;
q->Freeze();
q->select_plate(m_cur_slice_plate);
partplate_list.select_plate_view();
int ret = q->start_next_slice();
```

### `Plater::start_next_slice()` — `Plater.cpp:16193`
```cpp
int Plater::start_next_slice()
```
`update_background_process(true, false, false)` (note `switch_print = false`), then validates via `p->partplate_list.get_curr_plate()->can_slice()`; on failure sets `process_completed_with_error` and returns `-1` (`Plater.cpp:16205-16209`). On `!result` from `restart_background_process` it queues a synthetic `Finished` `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` (`Plater.cpp:16214-16220`). Returns `0` otherwise. **Does not touch Preview.**

### Slicing a *specific* plate
There is no "slice plate N" API. The only composite is:
- `Plater::select_plate(int plate_index, bool need_slice)` — `Plater.cpp:17664`. With `need_slice = true` and preview shown and the plate's apply invalidated / gcode empty, it does `p->m_slice_all = false; reset_gcode_toolpaths(); reslice();` (`Plater.cpp:17706-17713`). ## 2. BackgroundSlicingProcess

Header: `src/slic3r/GUI/BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp`.

**Start / stop / reset** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:130-136`):
```cpp
bool start();
bool stop();
bool reset();
```
- `start()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:510`. Returns `false` if `m_print->empty()` and the plate has no valid result; returns `false` if `this->running()`; **throws `Slic3r::RuntimeError("Cannot start a background task, the worker thread is not idle.")` if neither idle nor running** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:536`). Sets `m_state = STATE_STARTED` and installs `m_print->set_cancel_callback([this]{ this->stop_internal(); })`.
- `stop()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:546`. **Blocking**: `m_print->cancel(); m_condition.wait(lck, [this]{ return m_state == STATE_CANCELED; });` then `m_state = STATE_IDLE`. Returns `false` only if `m_state == STATE_INITIAL`; returns `true` otherwise — including when the process was already `STATE_FINISHED`. So `stop()`'s return value does **not** tell you whether you actually cancelled anything in flight.
- `stop_internal()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:589`, private, called from `Print::apply()` via the cancel callback; uses `m_print->cancel_internal()`, which suppresses the completion event (see below) and sets `m_internal_cancelled = true`.

**State queries** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:162-188`):
```cpp
enum State { STATE_INITIAL, STATE_IDLE, STATE_STARTED, STATE_RUNNING,
             STATE_FINISHED, STATE_CANCELED, STATE_EXIT, STATE_EXITED };
State state() const { return m_state; }
bool  idle()  const { return m_state == STATE_IDLE; }
bool  running() const { return m_state == STATE_STARTED || m_state == STATE_RUNNING
                            || m_state == STATE_FINISHED || m_state == STATE_CANCELED; }
bool  finished() const { return m_print->finished() && !m_gcode_result->moves.empty(); }
bool  is_internal_cancelled() { return m_internal_cancelled; }
```
Plus `empty()`, `validate(...)` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:145-148`), `get_current_plate()` / `set_current_plate()` (`:95-96`), `switch_print_preprocess()` / `can_switch_print()` (`:93-94`). `friend class GUI::Plater;` at `:192`, so `Plater` reaches privates.

**Event ids are injected by Plater, not owned by BSP** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:102-112`, wired at `Plater.cpp:4981-4998`):
```cpp
background_process.set_slicing_completed_event(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED);
background_process.set_finished_event(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED);
background_process.set_export_began_event(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN);
```

**wx event ids** (`Plater.cpp:191-194`):
```cpp
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE,    SlicingStatusEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED, wxCommandEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, SlicingProcessCompletedEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN,      wxCommandEvent);
```
There is no `EVT_SLICING_BEGAN`; `on_slicing_began()` (`Plater.cpp:9835`) is a direct call from `restart_background_process`.

**Bindings — today, only Plater::priv binds them:**
- `Plater.cpp:5000` — `this->q->Bind(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE, &priv::on_slicing_update, this);`
- `Plater.cpp:5295-5297`:
```cpp
q->Bind(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED, &priv::on_slicing_completed, this);
q->Bind(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, &priv::on_process_completed, this);
q->Bind(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN,      &priv::on_export_began, this);
```
Also `PartPlate.cpp:3456` constructs a `SlicingStatusEvent(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE, 0, status)` for progress from the plate's own slicing.

**Payloads**
- `SlicingStatusEvent` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:27-35`) carries `PrintBase::SlicingStatus status` — `percent`, `text`, `flags`, `warning_object_id`, `warning_step`, `message_type`. Consumed at `Plater.cpp:9710`.
- `EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED` is a bare `wxCommandEvent` — **no payload, no plate id, no success flag**. `on_slicing_completed` (`Plater.cpp:9793`) only refreshes shells, and returns early during slice-all for non-final plates.
- `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:37-68`) carries `StatusType m_status {Finished, Cancelled, Error}` and `std::exception_ptr m_exception`. Accessors: `status()`, `finished()`, `success()`, `cancelled()`, `error()`, `critical_error()` (`.cpp:42`), `invalidate_plater()` (`.cpp:55`), `rethrow_exception()`, `format_error_message()` (`.cpp:73`). **It carries no plate identity and no handle** — the recipient must infer the plate from `background_process.get_current_plate()` / `partplate_list.get_curr_plate_index()`.

**Failure vs cancellation** — decided on the worker thread at `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:344-354`:
```cpp
m_state = m_print->canceled() ? STATE_CANCELED : STATE_FINISHED;
if (m_print->cancel_status() != Print::CANCELED_INTERNAL) {
    SlicingProcessCompletedEvent evt(m_event_finished_id, 0,
        (m_state == STATE_CANCELED) ? SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Cancelled :
        exception ? SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Error : SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Finished, exception);
    wxQueueEvent(GUI::wxGetApp().mainframe->m_plater, evt.Clone());
}
else {
    m_internal_cancelled = true;
}
```
Two consequences that matter for an action handle:
1. **Cancellation wins over error**: if the print was cancelled, an exception that was also captured is reported as `Cancelled`, not `Error`.
2. **`CANCELED_INTERNAL` produces no event at all.** An internal cancel (from `Print::apply()`) is silent; the only trace is `is_internal_cancelled()`, which `update_background_process` then converts into a synthetic `Cancelled` `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` at `Plater.cpp:8109-8118`. **A terminal-state reader that waits on `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` alone can hang on an internal cancel that never reaches `update_background_process`.**

Also note `m_ignore_event` (`Plater.cpp:4371`) — `on_process_completed` swallows exactly one event when set (`Plater.cpp:9912-9916`). Nothing in the current tree ever sets it to `true`; it is only read and reset.

```cpp
OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::SliceState OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::current_slice_state() const
{
    SliceState state;
    // Whether a slice is running is part of what the plate holds, not merely
    // progress: starting one on an already-invalid plate changes neither the
    // valid flag nor the result id, so without it that transition publishes
    // nothing and no consumer ever learns the slice began.
    const bool slicing = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing();
    PartPlateList& plates = m_plater.get_partplate_list();
    for (int index = 0; index < plates.get_plate_count(); ++index) {
        PartPlate* plate = plates.get_plate(index);
        if (plate == nullptr) continue;
        const bool sliced = plate->is_slice_result_valid();
        const std::uint64_t result = sliced && !slicing && plate->get_slice_result() ?
            plate->get_slice_result()->id : 0;
        state.emplace(plate->id().id, PlateSlice{sliced, result, slicing});
    }
    return state;
}

void OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::on_slice_status_changed(wxCommandEvent& event)
{
    event.Skip();
    wxASSERT(wxIsMainThread());
    // This event also fires whenever the native toolbar re-evaluates whether
    // Slice and Print are enabled, ...
    SliceState state = current_slice_state();
    if (state == m_known_slice_state)
        return;
    // A plate that held a slice and no longer does was invalidated by whatever
    // the person just did. ...
    for (const auto& [id, now] : state) {
        const auto before = m_known_slice_state.find(id);
        if (before != m_known_slice_state.end() && before->second.sliced && !now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by[id] = m_last_change_reason;
        else if (now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by.erase(id);
    }
    m_known_slice_state = std::move(state);
    publish_change(WorkspaceChangeReasons::Plates);
}
```

## 4. How `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter` learns a plate is sliced

Two mechanisms: the **event** in §3 advances the revision; the **snapshot** computes the fields. All of `sliced`, `estimate`, `estimate_status`, `invalidated_by` are computed in `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::snapshot()`, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:264-286`:
```cpp
projected_plate.sliced = plate->is_slice_result_valid();
const std::uint64_t plate_key = plate->id().id;
if (projected_plate.sliced && !m_plater.is_background_process_slicing() && plate->get_slice_result()) {
    projected_plate.estimate        = estimate_of(*plate->get_slice_result());
    projected_plate.estimate_status = EstimateStatus::Current;
    // The figure this plate can currently defend, kept so a slice in
    // flight or an invalidated one still has something to show.
    if (projected_plate.estimate) m_last_estimate[plate_key] = *projected_plate.estimate;
} else if (const auto remembered = m_last_estimate.find(plate_key); remembered != m_last_estimate.end()) {
    projected_plate.estimate        = remembered->second;
    projected_plate.estimate_status = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing() ?
        EstimateStatus::Recomputing : EstimateStatus::Stale;
    if (projected_plate.estimate_status == EstimateStatus::Stale) {
        if (const auto why = m_invalidated_by.find(plate_key); why != m_invalidated_by.end())
            projected_plate.invalidated_by = why->second;
    }
}
```

`estimate_of` — `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:79-107` — reads `GCodeProcessorResult::print_statistics`, `modes[ETimeMode::Normal].time`, `total_volumes_per_extruder × filament_densities × 0.001`, and `filament_costs`. Returns `std::nullopt` if any extruder lacks a density, or if time is 0 and grams ≤ 0.

`m_last_change_reason` (the source of `invalidated_by`) is set in `on_project_state_changed`, `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:508-519`:
```cpp
if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Transform))     m_last_change_reason = "you moved the object";
else if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Objects))  m_last_change_reason = "the objects changed";
else if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Settings)) m_last_change_reason = "a setting changed";
else                                                  m_last_change_reason.clear();
```

Target struct — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp:102-124`: `enum class EstimateStatus { Current, Recomputing, Stale }`, `WorkspacePlate::sliced` (":True when this plate holds a currently valid slice result. Derived from the authoritative plate state on every snapshot, never cached."), `estimate`, `estimate_status`, `invalidated_by`.

**Note the one asymmetry that matters to you:** `is_background_process_slicing()` is a *global* flag, not per-plate. During slice-all, every already-sliced plate's estimate flips to `Recomputing`, not just the plate being sliced.

## 6. Cancellation

**The real path.** All GUI entry points funnel into `Plater::cancel_slicing()` — `Plater.cpp:18345-18351`:
```cpp
bool Plater::cancel_slicing()
{
    if (p->background_process.idle())
        return false;
    p->background_process.stop();
    return true;
}
```
Callers:
- The slicing-progress notification's cancel button — `Plater.cpp:10907-10911` (`init_slicing_progress_notification(cancel_callback)`).
- The fork header's Cancel action — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:462`: `case PrintAction::Cancel: m_plater.cancel_slicing(); return;`

Two other places call `background_process.stop()` directly, bypassing `cancel_slicing()`:
- `Plater.cpp:7767` in `schedule_auto_reslice_if_needed()` — sets `auto_reslice_after_cancel = true` first, so the restart happens in `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10119-10122`.
- `Plater.cpp:11366` in `show_publish_dlg(false)`.
- `Plater.cpp:9938` in `on_process_completed` itself — the confirmatory stop after the thread already finished.

**Does it report whether cancellation won the race? No, and there are three separate reasons:**

1. `cancel_slicing()` returns `false` only for `idle()`. If the slice had already reached `STATE_FINISHED` a microsecond earlier, `idle()` is still false (`running()` includes `STATE_FINISHED` and `STATE_CANCELED`, `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:180`), so `stop()` runs, takes the `m_state == STATE_FINISHED` branch (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:565-568`) which just resets to `STATE_IDLE`, and `cancel_slicing()` returns `true` — for a slice that in fact completed successfully.

2. `BackgroundSlicingProcess::stop()` itself returns `true` in both the "actually cancelled a running task" and the "it was already finished" branches. Its `false` means only `STATE_INITIAL`.

```cpp
OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::SliceState OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::current_slice_state() const
{
    SliceState state;
    // Whether a slice is running is part of what the plate holds, not merely
    // progress: starting one on an already-invalid plate changes neither the
    // valid flag nor the result id, so without it that transition publishes
    // nothing and no consumer ever learns the slice began.
    const bool slicing = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing();
    PartPlateList& plates = m_plater.get_partplate_list();
    for (int index = 0; index < plates.get_plate_count(); ++index) {
        PartPlate* plate = plates.get_plate(index);
        if (plate == nullptr) continue;
        const bool sliced = plate->is_slice_result_valid();
        const std::uint64_t result = sliced && !slicing && plate->get_slice_result() ?
            plate->get_slice_result()->id : 0;
        state.emplace(plate->id().id, PlateSlice{sliced, result, slicing});
    }
    return state;
}

void OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::on_slice_status_changed(wxCommandEvent& event)
{
    event.Skip();
    wxASSERT(wxIsMainThread());
    // This event also fires whenever the native toolbar re-evaluates whether
    // Slice and Print are enabled, ...
    SliceState state = current_slice_state();
    if (state == m_known_slice_state)
        return;
    // A plate that held a slice and no longer does was invalidated by whatever
    // the person just did. ...
    for (const auto& [id, now] : state) {
        const auto before = m_known_slice_state.find(id);
        if (before != m_known_slice_state.end() && before->second.sliced && !now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by[id] = m_last_change_reason;
        else if (now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by.erase(id);
    }
    m_known_slice_state = std::move(state);
    publish_change(WorkspaceChangeReasons::Plates);
}
```

## 6. Cancellation

**The real path.** All GUI entry points funnel into `Plater::cancel_slicing()` — `Plater.cpp:18345-18351`:
```cpp
bool Plater::cancel_slicing()
{
    if (p->background_process.idle())
        return false;
    p->background_process.stop();
    return true;
}
```
Callers:
- The slicing-progress notification's cancel button — `Plater.cpp:10907-10911` (`init_slicing_progress_notification(cancel_callback)`).
- The fork header's Cancel action — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:462`: `case PrintAction::Cancel: m_plater.cancel_slicing(); return;`

Two other places call `background_process.stop()` directly, bypassing `cancel_slicing()`:
- `Plater.cpp:7767` in `schedule_auto_reslice_if_needed()` — sets `auto_reslice_after_cancel = true` first, so the restart happens in `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10119-10122`.
- `Plater.cpp:11366` in `show_publish_dlg(false)`.
- `Plater.cpp:9938` in `on_process_completed` itself — the confirmatory stop after the thread already finished.

**Does it report whether cancellation won the race? No, and there are three separate reasons:**

1. `cancel_slicing()` returns `false` only for `idle()`. If the slice had already reached `STATE_FINISHED` a microsecond earlier, `idle()` is still false (`running()` includes `STATE_FINISHED` and `STATE_CANCELED`, `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:180`), so `stop()` runs, takes the `m_state == STATE_FINISHED` branch (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:565-568`) which just resets to `STATE_IDLE`, and `cancel_slicing()` returns `true` — for a slice that in fact completed successfully.

2. `BackgroundSlicingProcess::stop()` itself returns `true` in both the "actually cancelled a running task" and the "it was already finished" branches. Its `false` means only `STATE_INITIAL`.

3. The worker already decided the outcome before the UI thread's `stop()` returns. `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:344`: `m_state = m_print->canceled() ? STATE_CANCELED : STATE_FINISHED;`. If `m_print->cancel()` landed after the last `throw_if_canceled()` checkpoint, the queued `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` carries `Finished`, not `Cancelled` — and `on_process_completed` will then mark the plate valid via `update_slice_result_valid_state(evt.success())` (`Plater.cpp:9984-9985`).

The only authoritative statement of who won is the `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::status()` that arrives afterwards — with the caveats from §2 that an internal cancel emits nothing, and that `update_background_process` can inject a synthetic `Cancelled` that no user cancellation produced (`Plater.cpp:8109-8118`).

On the cancelled branch, `on_process_completed` does `notification_manager->set_slicing_progress_canceled(_u8L("Slicing Canceled"))` and forces `is_finished = true` (`Plater.cpp:9977-9982`) — so a cancel inside a slice-all **stops the whole run**, it does not skip to the next plate.</result>

## 6. Cancellation

**The real path.** All GUI entry points funnel into `Plater::cancel_slicing()` — `Plater.cpp:18345-18351`:
```cpp
bool Plater::cancel_slicing()
{
    if (p->background_process.idle())
        return false;
    p->background_process.stop();
    return true;
}
```
Callers:
- The slicing-progress notification's cancel button — `Plater.cpp:10907-10911` (`init_slicing_progress_notification(cancel_callback)`).
- The fork header's Cancel action — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:462`: `case PrintAction::Cancel: m_plater.cancel_slicing(); return;`

Two other places call `background_process.stop()` directly, bypassing `cancel_slicing()`:
- `Plater.cpp:7767` in `schedule_auto_reslice_if_needed()` — sets `auto_reslice_after_cancel = true` first, so the restart happens in `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10119-10122`.
- `Plater.cpp:11366` in `show_publish_dlg(false)`.
- `Plater.cpp:9938` in `on_process_completed` itself — the confirmatory stop after the thread already finished.

**Does it report whether cancellation won the race? No, and there are three separate reasons:**

1. `cancel_slicing()` returns `false` only for `idle()`. If the slice had already reached `STATE_FINISHED` a microsecond earlier, `idle()` is still false (`running()` includes `STATE_FINISHED` and `STATE_CANCELED`, `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:180`), so `stop()` runs, takes the `m_state == STATE_FINISHED` branch (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:565-568`) which just resets to `STATE_IDLE`, and `cancel_slicing()` returns `true` — for a slice that in fact completed successfully.

2. `BackgroundSlicingProcess::stop()` itself returns `true` in both the "actually cancelled a running task" and the "it was already finished" branches. Its `false` means only `STATE_INITIAL`.

3. The worker already decided the outcome before the UI thread's `stop()` returns. `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:344`: `m_state = m_print->canceled() ? STATE_CANCELED : STATE_FINISHED;`. If `m_print->cancel()` landed after the last `throw_if_canceled()` checkpoint, the queued `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` carries `Finished`, not `Cancelled` — and `on_process_completed` will then mark the plate valid via `update_slice_result_valid_state(evt.success())` (`Plater.cpp:9984-9985`).

The only authoritative statement of who won is the `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::status()` that arrives afterwards — with the caveats from §2 that an internal cancel emits nothing, and that `update_background_process` can inject a synthetic `Cancelled` that no user cancellation produced (`Plater.cpp:8109-8118`).

On the cancelled branch, `on_process_completed` does `notification_manager->set_slicing_progress_canceled(_u8L("Slicing Canceled"))` and forces `is_finished = true` (`Plater.cpp:9977-9982`) — so a cancel inside a slice-all **stops the whole run**, it does not skip to the next plate.</result>

## 2. BackgroundSlicingProcess

Header: `src/slic3r/GUI/BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp`.

**Start / stop / reset** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:130-136`):
```cpp
bool start();
bool stop();
bool reset();
```
- `start()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:510`. Returns `false` if `m_print->empty()` and the plate has no valid result; returns `false` if `this->running()`; **throws `Slic3r::RuntimeError("Cannot start a background task, the worker thread is not idle.")` if neither idle nor running** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:536`). Sets `m_state = STATE_STARTED` and installs `m_print->set_cancel_callback([this]{ this->stop_internal(); })`.
- `stop()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:546`. **Blocking**: `m_print->cancel(); m_condition.wait(lck, [this]{ return m_state == STATE_CANCELED; });` then `m_state = STATE_IDLE`. Returns `false` only if `m_state == STATE_INITIAL`; returns `true` otherwise — including when the process was already `STATE_FINISHED`. So `stop()`'s return value does **not** tell you whether you actually cancelled anything in flight.
- `stop_internal()` — `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:589`, private, called from `Print::apply()` via the cancel callback; uses `m_print->cancel_internal()`, which suppresses the completion event (see below) and sets `m_internal_cancelled = true`.

**State queries** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:162-188`):
```cpp
enum State { STATE_INITIAL, STATE_IDLE, STATE_STARTED, STATE_RUNNING,
             STATE_FINISHED, STATE_CANCELED, STATE_EXIT, STATE_EXITED };
State state() const { return m_state; }
bool  idle()  const { return m_state == STATE_IDLE; }
bool  running() const { return m_state == STATE_STARTED || m_state == STATE_RUNNING
                            || m_state == STATE_FINISHED || m_state == STATE_CANCELED; }
bool  finished() const { return m_print->finished() && !m_gcode_result->moves.empty(); }
bool  is_internal_cancelled() { return m_internal_cancelled; }
```
Plus `empty()`, `validate(...)` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:145-148`), `get_current_plate()` / `set_current_plate()` (`:95-96`), `switch_print_preprocess()` / `can_switch_print()` (`:93-94`). `friend class GUI::Plater;` at `:192`, so `Plater` reaches privates.

**Event ids are injected by Plater, not owned by BSP** (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:102-112`, wired at `Plater.cpp:4981-4998`):
```cpp
background_process.set_slicing_completed_event(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED);
background_process.set_finished_event(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED);
background_process.set_export_began_event(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN);
```

**wx event ids** (`Plater.cpp:191-194`):
```cpp
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE,    SlicingStatusEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED, wxCommandEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, SlicingProcessCompletedEvent);
wxDEFINE_EVENT(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN,      wxCommandEvent);
```
There is no `EVT_SLICING_BEGAN`; `on_slicing_began()` (`Plater.cpp:9835`) is a direct call from `restart_background_process`.

**Bindings — today, only Plater::priv binds them:**
- `Plater.cpp:5000` — `this->q->Bind(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE, &priv::on_slicing_update, this);`
- `Plater.cpp:5295-5297`:
```cpp
q->Bind(EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED, &priv::on_slicing_completed, this);
q->Bind(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, &priv::on_process_completed, this);
q->Bind(EVT_EXPORT_BEGAN,      &priv::on_export_began, this);
```
Also `PartPlate.cpp:3456` constructs a `SlicingStatusEvent(EVT_SLICING_UPDATE, 0, status)` for progress from the plate's own slicing.

**Payloads**
- `SlicingStatusEvent` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:27-35`) carries `PrintBase::SlicingStatus status` — `percent`, `text`, `flags`, `warning_object_id`, `warning_step`, `message_type`. Consumed at `Plater.cpp:9710`.
- `EVT_SLICING_COMPLETED` is a bare `wxCommandEvent` — **no payload, no plate id, no success flag**. `on_slicing_completed` (`Plater.cpp:9793`) only refreshes shells, and returns early during slice-all for non-final plates.
- `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent` (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:37-68`) carries `StatusType m_status {Finished, Cancelled, Error}` and `std::exception_ptr m_exception`. Accessors: `status()`, `finished()`, `success()`, `cancelled()`, `error()`, `critical_error()` (`.cpp:42`), `invalidate_plater()` (`.cpp:55`), `rethrow_exception()`, `format_error_message()` (`.cpp:73`). **It carries no plate identity and no handle** — the recipient must infer the plate from `background_process.get_current_plate()` / `partplate_list.get_curr_plate_index()`.

**Failure vs cancellation** — decided on the worker thread at `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:344-354`:
```cpp
m_state = m_print->canceled() ? STATE_CANCELED : STATE_FINISHED;
if (m_print->cancel_status() != Print::CANCELED_INTERNAL) {
    SlicingProcessCompletedEvent evt(m_event_finished_id, 0,
        (m_state == STATE_CANCELED) ? SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Cancelled :
        exception ? SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Error : SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::Finished, exception);
    wxQueueEvent(GUI::wxGetApp().mainframe->m_plater, evt.Clone());
}
else {
    m_internal_cancelled = true;
}
```
Two consequences that matter for an action handle:
1. **Cancellation wins over error**: if the print was cancelled, an exception that was also captured is reported as `Cancelled`, not `Error`.
2. **`CANCELED_INTERNAL` produces no event at all.** An internal cancel (from `Print::apply()`) is silent; the only trace is `is_internal_cancelled()`, which `update_background_process` then converts into a synthetic `Cancelled` `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` at `Plater.cpp:8109-8118`. **A terminal-state reader that waits on `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` alone can hang on an internal cancel that never reaches `update_background_process`.**

Also note `m_ignore_event` (`Plater.cpp:4371`) — `on_process_completed` swallows exactly one event when set (`Plater.cpp:9912-9916`). Nothing in the current tree ever sets it to `true`; it is only read and reset.

```cpp
OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::SliceState OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::current_slice_state() const
{
    SliceState state;
    // Whether a slice is running is part of what the plate holds, not merely
    // progress: starting one on an already-invalid plate changes neither the
    // valid flag nor the result id, so without it that transition publishes
    // nothing and no consumer ever learns the slice began.
    const bool slicing = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing();
    PartPlateList& plates = m_plater.get_partplate_list();
    for (int index = 0; index < plates.get_plate_count(); ++index) {
        PartPlate* plate = plates.get_plate(index);
        if (plate == nullptr) continue;
        const bool sliced = plate->is_slice_result_valid();
        const std::uint64_t result = sliced && !slicing && plate->get_slice_result() ?
            plate->get_slice_result()->id : 0;
        state.emplace(plate->id().id, PlateSlice{sliced, result, slicing});
    }
    return state;
}

void OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::on_slice_status_changed(wxCommandEvent& event)
{
    event.Skip();
    wxASSERT(wxIsMainThread());
    // This event also fires whenever the native toolbar re-evaluates whether
    // Slice and Print are enabled, ...
    SliceState state = current_slice_state();
    if (state == m_known_slice_state)
        return;
    // A plate that held a slice and no longer does was invalidated by whatever
    // the person just did. ...
    for (const auto& [id, now] : state) {
        const auto before = m_known_slice_state.find(id);
        if (before != m_known_slice_state.end() && before->second.sliced && !now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by[id] = m_last_change_reason;
        else if (now.sliced)
            m_invalidated_by.erase(id);
    }
    m_known_slice_state = std::move(state);
    publish_change(WorkspaceChangeReasons::Plates);
}
```

## 4. How `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter` learns a plate is sliced

Two mechanisms: the **event** in §3 advances the revision; the **snapshot** computes the fields. All of `sliced`, `estimate`, `estimate_status`, `invalidated_by` are computed in `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::snapshot()`, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:264-286`:
```cpp
projected_plate.sliced = plate->is_slice_result_valid();
const std::uint64_t plate_key = plate->id().id;
if (projected_plate.sliced && !m_plater.is_background_process_slicing() && plate->get_slice_result()) {
    projected_plate.estimate        = estimate_of(*plate->get_slice_result());
    projected_plate.estimate_status = EstimateStatus::Current;
    // The figure this plate can currently defend, kept so a slice in
    // flight or an invalidated one still has something to show.
    if (projected_plate.estimate) m_last_estimate[plate_key] = *projected_plate.estimate;
} else if (const auto remembered = m_last_estimate.find(plate_key); remembered != m_last_estimate.end()) {
    projected_plate.estimate        = remembered->second;
    projected_plate.estimate_status = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing() ?
        EstimateStatus::Recomputing : EstimateStatus::Stale;
    if (projected_plate.estimate_status == EstimateStatus::Stale) {
        if (const auto why = m_invalidated_by.find(plate_key); why != m_invalidated_by.end())
            projected_plate.invalidated_by = why->second;
    }
}
```

`estimate_of` — `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:79-107` — reads `GCodeProcessorResult::print_statistics`, `modes[ETimeMode::Normal].time`, `total_volumes_per_extruder × filament_densities × 0.001`, and `filament_costs`. Returns `std::nullopt` if any extruder lacks a density, or if time is 0 and grams ≤ 0.

`m_last_change_reason` (the source of `invalidated_by`) is set in `on_project_state_changed`, `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:508-519`:
```cpp
if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Transform))     m_last_change_reason = "you moved the object";
else if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Objects))  m_last_change_reason = "the objects changed";
else if (touched(ProjectStateChangeReason::Settings)) m_last_change_reason = "a setting changed";
else                                                  m_last_change_reason.clear();
```

Target struct — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp:102-124`: `enum class EstimateStatus { Current, Recomputing, Stale }`, `WorkspacePlate::sliced` (":True when this plate holds a currently valid slice result. Derived from the authoritative plate state on every snapshot, never cached."), `estimate`, `estimate_status`, `invalidated_by`.

**Note the one asymmetry that matters to you:** `is_background_process_slicing()` is a *global* flag, not per-plate. During slice-all, every already-sliced plate's estimate flips to `Recomputing`, not just the plate being sliced.

## 6. Cancellation

**The real path.** All GUI entry points funnel into `Plater::cancel_slicing()` — `Plater.cpp:18345-18351`:
```cpp
bool Plater::cancel_slicing()
{
    if (p->background_process.idle())
        return false;
    p->background_process.stop();
    return true;
}
```
Callers:
- The slicing-progress notification's cancel button — `Plater.cpp:10907-10911` (`init_slicing_progress_notification(cancel_callback)`).
- The fork header's Cancel action — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:462`: `case PrintAction::Cancel: m_plater.cancel_slicing(); return;`

Two other places call `background_process.stop()` directly, bypassing `cancel_slicing()`:
- `Plater.cpp:7767` in `schedule_auto_reslice_if_needed()` — sets `auto_reslice_after_cancel = true` first, so the restart happens in `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10119-10122`.
- `Plater.cpp:11366` in `show_publish_dlg(false)`.
- `Plater.cpp:9938` in `on_process_completed` itself — the confirmatory stop after the thread already finished.

**Does it report whether cancellation won the race? No, and there are three separate reasons:**

1. `cancel_slicing()` returns `false` only for `idle()`. If the slice had already reached `STATE_FINISHED` a microsecond earlier, `idle()` is still false (`running()` includes `STATE_FINISHED` and `STATE_CANCELED`, `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:180`), so `stop()` runs, takes the `m_state == STATE_FINISHED` branch (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:565-568`) which just resets to `STATE_IDLE`, and `cancel_slicing()` returns `true` — for a slice that in fact completed successfully.

```cpp
{
```

```cpp
    // Whether a slice is running is part of what the plate holds, not merely
    // progress: starting one on an already-invalid plate changes neither the
    // valid flag nor the result id, so without it that transition publishes
    // nothing and no consumer ever learns the slice began.
    const bool slicing = m_plater.is_background_process_slicing();

            plate->get_slice_result()->id : 0;
        state.emplace(plate->id().id, PlateSlice{sliced, result, slicing});

    return state;
}
```

## 5. Can anything distinguish "GUI started this slice" from "a tool started this slice"?

**No. Nothing in the tree carries slice provenance.** The complete set of slicing-related state:

| symbol | location | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| `Plater::priv::m_is_slicing` | `Plater.cpp:4373` | a slice sequence is in flight (spans all plates of a slice-all) |
| `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()` | `Plater.hpp:770`, `Plater.cpp:18340-18343` | `return p->m_is_slicing;` — the predicate to reuse |
| `BackgroundSlicingProcess::running()/idle()/state()/finished()` | `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:178-187` | thread state only |
| `Plater::priv::m_slice_all` | `Plater.cpp:4372` | slice-all in progress |
| `Plater::priv::m_cur_slice_plate` | `Plater.cpp:4378` | which plate slice-all is on |
| `Plater::priv::m_slice_all_only_has_gcode` | `Plater.cpp:4380` | gcode.3mf variant |
| `Plater::priv::process_completed_with_error` | plate index or `-1` | last plate that failed validation/slicing |
| `Plater::priv::m_ignore_event` | `Plater.cpp:4371` | swallow the next `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`; never set today |
| `Plater::priv::auto_reslice_pending` / `auto_reslice_after_cancel` | `Plater.cpp:4374-4375` | fork's auto-slice bookkeeping |
| `PartPlate::can_slice()` | `PartPlate.hpp:433-436` | `return m_ready_for_slice && !m_apply_invalid;` |
| `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` | `PartPlate.hpp:453-456` | `return m_slice_result_valid;` |
| `PartPlate::is_slice_result_ready_for_print()` | `PartPlate.hpp:459-469` | valid **and** `!toolpath_outside && gcode_check_result.error_code == 0 && !filament_printable_reuslt.has_value()` |
| `PartPlate::is_slice_result_ready_for_export()` | `PartPlate.hpp:471-473` | `is_slice_result_ready_for_print() && has_printable_instances()` |
| `PartPlate::get_slice_result()` | `PartPlate.hpp:491` | `GCodeProcessorResult*`, whose `->id` is used as the fork's result identity |
| `PartPlate::get_slicing_percent()` | `PartPlate.hpp:483` | per-plate progress |

`MachineObject::is_in_printing_status(std::string status)` (`DeviceManager.hpp:821`, `DeviceManager.cpp:2301`) is about the **physical printer**, not slicing — do not reuse it here.

The fork's own reusable readiness predicate is `StatusRow::action_state()` — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:176-208` — which already assembles `slicing / sliced / can_slice / can_slice_all / can_print / can_export / sliced_count / plate_count` from exactly those primitives, including the `editable = !only_gcode_mode() && !using_exported_file()` gate at `StatusRow.cpp:184`. And `StatusRow::print_target_identity()` (`StatusRow.cpp:222-229`) is the fork's existing pattern for a stable "this plate, this result" tuple:
```cpp

        plate && plate->is_slice_result_valid() && !m_plater.is_background_process_slicing() && plate->get_slice_result() ?
            plate->get_slice_result()->id : 0};
```

Because there is no provenance, a slice you did not start can be indistinguishable from yours. The slices the GUI can start without a user click are: `set_current_panel` on Preview entry (`Plater.cpp:9155-9174`), `Plater::select_plate(..., need_slice=true)` (`Plater.cpp:17706-17713`), `check_ams_status_impl`'s "Sync now" re-post (`Plater.cpp:11114-11120`), `GCodeViewer.cpp:2872`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp:8857`, `MainFrame.cpp:708` (Ctrl+R), `MainFrame.cpp:1920-1922`, `Plater.cpp:18066`, and the fork's own `trigger_auto_reslice_now()` (`Plater.cpp:7787`).

---

## 6. Cancellation

**The real path.** All GUI entry points funnel into `Plater::cancel_slicing()` — `Plater.cpp:18345-18351`:
```cpp
bool Plater::cancel_slicing()
{
    if (p->background_process.idle())
        return false;
    p->background_process.stop();
    return true;
}
```
Callers:
- The slicing-progress notification's cancel button — `Plater.cpp:10907-10911` (`init_slicing_progress_notification(cancel_callback)`).
- The fork header's Cancel action — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:462`: `case PrintAction::Cancel: m_plater.cancel_slicing(); return;`

Two other places call `background_process.stop()` directly, bypassing `cancel_slicing()`:
- `Plater.cpp:7767` in `schedule_auto_reslice_if_needed()` — sets `auto_reslice_after_cancel = true` first, so the restart happens in `on_process_completed` at `Plater.cpp:10119-10122`.
- `Plater.cpp:11366` in `show_publish_dlg(false)`.
- `Plater.cpp:9938` in `on_process_completed` itself — the confirmatory stop after the thread already finished.

**Does it report whether cancellation won the race? No, and there are three separate reasons:**

1. `cancel_slicing()` returns `false` only for `idle()`. If the slice had already reached `STATE_FINISHED` a microsecond earlier, `idle()` is still false (`running()` includes `STATE_FINISHED` and `STATE_CANCELED`, `BackgroundSlicingProcess.hpp:180`), so `stop()` runs, takes the `m_state == STATE_FINISHED` branch (`BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:565-568`) which just resets to `STATE_IDLE`, and `cancel_slicing()` returns `true` — for a slice that in fact completed successfully.

2. `BackgroundSlicingProcess::stop()` itself returns `true` in both the "actually cancelled a running task" and the "it was already finished" branches. Its `false` means only `STATE_INITIAL`.

3. The worker already decided the outcome before the UI thread's `stop()` returns. `BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:344`: `m_state = m_print->canceled() ? STATE_CANCELED : STATE_FINISHED;`. If `m_print->cancel()` landed after the last `throw_if_canceled()` checkpoint, the queued `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` carries `Finished`, not `Cancelled` — and `on_process_completed` will then mark the plate valid via `update_slice_result_valid_state(evt.success())` (`Plater.cpp:9984-9985`).

The only authoritative statement of who won is the `SlicingProcessCompletedEvent::status()` that arrives afterwards — with the caveats from §2 that an internal cancel emits nothing, and that `update_background_process` can inject a synthetic `Cancelled` that no user cancellation produced (`Plater.cpp:8109-8118`).

On the cancelled branch, `on_process_completed` does `notification_manager->set_slicing_progress_canceled(_u8L("Slicing Canceled"))` and forces `is_finished = true` (`Plater.cpp:9977-9982`) — so a cancel inside a slice-all **stops the whole run**, it does not skip to the next plate.</result>

### Owners (libslic3r)

Two distinct owners, both filled at G-code export time:

**A. `GCodeProcessorResult::print_statistics` — per-extruder, volume-based.** `C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\GCode\GCodeProcessor.hpp:46-113`:

```cpp

unsigned int                                        total_extruder_changes;
```

`Mode` (`GCodeProcessor.hpp:55-67`) is `{ float time; float prepare_time; std::vector<std::pair<CustomGCode::Type, std::pair<float,float>>> custom_gcode_times; }`. Time is **seconds**; volumes are **mm³**. Keys of all the `*_per_extruder` maps are **filament/extruder indices, 0-based**.

Filled in `GCodeProcessor::update_estimated_times_stats()`, `C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\GCode\GCodeProcessor.cpp:6016-6038`:

```cpp
update_mode(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Normal);
if (m_time_processor.machines[static_cast<size_t>(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Stealth)].enabled)
    update_mode(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Stealth);
else
    m_result.print_statistics.modes[static_cast<size_t>(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Stealth)].reset();
m_result.print_statistics.volumes_per_color_change  = m_used_filaments.volumes_per_color_change;
m_result.print_statistics.model_volumes_per_extruder      = m_used_filaments.model_volumes_per_filament;
m_result.print_statistics.wipe_tower_volumes_per_extruder = m_used_filaments.wipe_tower_volumes_per_filament;
m_result.print_statistics.support_volumes_per_extruder = m_used_filaments.support_volumes_per_filament;
m_result.print_statistics.flush_per_filament      = m_used_filaments.flush_per_filament;
m_result.print_statistics.used_filaments_per_role   = m_used_filaments.filaments_per_role;
m_result.print_statistics.total_volumes_per_extruder = m_used_filaments.total_volumes_per_filament;
```

The per-filament conversion inputs also live on the result (`GCodeProcessor.hpp:252-255`): `filament_diameters`, `filament_densities`, `filament_costs` — all `std::vector<float>` indexed by filament id. `filament_costs` is price **per kg**; `filament_densities` is g/cm³.

**B. `PrintStatistics` on the `Print` — totals only.** `C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\Print.hpp:789-839`:

```cpp

std::string                     estimated_silent_print_time;
```

Note `filament_stats` is misnamed: it is set to **volumes**, not weights — `C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\GCode.cpp:1940`: `print_statistics.filament_stats = result.print_statistics.model_volumes_per_extruder;`. It is the *only* per-extruder field on `PrintStatistics`; everything else there is a plate total.

### Fill order (matters — two passes, one overwrites the other)

Pass 1, while writing G-code: `GCode.cpp:3525-3532` calls `DoExport::update_print_stats_and_format_filament_stats(...)` (`GCode.cpp:2313-2372`), which starts with `print_statistics.clear();` (`GCode.cpp:2322`), sets `total_toolchanges` (`:2323`), and accumulates `total_weight`, `total_cost`, `total_used_filament`, `total_extruded_volume`, `total_wipe_tower_filament`, `total_wipe_tower_cost` from `Extruder` objects (`:2350-2361`). Then `GCode.cpp:3533` sets `initial_tool`.

Pass 2, after processing: `GCode.cpp:2176` calls `DoExport::update_print_estimated_stats(...)` (`GCode.cpp:1904-1941`), which **overwrites** four of those from the processor result:

```cpp
double normal_print_time = result.print_statistics.modes[static_cast<size_t>(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Normal)].time;
print_statistics.estimated_normal_print_time = get_time_dhms(normal_print_time);
...
for (auto volume : result.print_statistics.total_volumes_per_extruder) {
    total_extruded_volume += volume.second;
    size_t extruder_id = volume.first;
    auto extruder = std::find_if(extruders.begin(), extruders.end(), [extruder_id](const Extruder& extr) {return extr.id() == extruder_id; });
    if (extruder == extruders.end())
        continue;
    double s = PI * sqr(0.5* extruder->filament_diameter());
    double weight = volume.second * extruder->filament_density() * 0.001;
    total_used_filament += volume.second/s;
```

- `PrintStatistics::total_cost` **includes machine time cost** (`time_cost` × hours). `GCodeProcessorResult`-derived cost does not.

- **`total_cost` is polluted by `time_cost`** (`GCode.cpp:1933`), so it can be non-zero with every filament unpriced.
- **Stealth/silent time**: `modes[Stealth]` is `reset()` to 0 when the stealth estimator is off (`GCodeProcessor.cpp:6029`); `estimated_silent_print_time` is the string `"N/A"`.

- **`filament_densities` / `filament_costs` may be shorter than the highest extruder index** — JusPrin's `estimate_of` bails out for exactly that reason (see §5).

## 2. Orca's own warnings for a sliced plate

Two *entirely separate* warning systems.

### System A: `PrintStateBase` step warnings (object-level and print-level)

`C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\PrintBase.hpp:54-57`:
```cpp
enum class WarningLevel {
    NON_CRITICAL,
    CRITICAL
};
```

`PrintBase.hpp:78-98`:
```cpp
struct Warning
{
    // Critical warnings will be displayed on G-code export in a modal dialog, so that the user cannot miss them.
    WarningLevel    level;
    // If the warning is not current, then it is in an unknown state. It may or may not be valid.
    bool 			current;
    // Message to be shown to the user, UTF8, localized.
    std::string     message;
    // If message_id == 0, then the message is expected to identify the warning uniquely.
    int 			message_id;
};

struct StateWithWarnings : public StateWithTimeStamp
{
    void 	mark_warnings_non_current() { for (auto &w : warnings) w.current = false; }
    std::vector<Warning>    warnings;
};
```

There is **no `print->warnings()` accessor**. Warnings are stored *per milestone step*, and the only read path is:

- print-level: `PrintBaseWithState::step_state_with_warnings(PrintStepEnum step)` — `PrintBase.hpp:587`
- object-level: `PrintObjectBaseWithState::step_state_with_warnings(PrintObjectStepEnum step)` — `PrintBase.hpp:634`

Steps to enumerate: `enum PrintStep { psWipeTower/psToolOrdering, psSkirtBrim/psSlicingFinished, psGCodeExport, psConflictCheck, psCount }` (`C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\Print.hpp:78-91`) and `enum PrintObjectStep { posSlice, posPerimeters, posEstimateCurledExtrusions, posPrepareInfill, posInfill, posIroning, posContouring, posSupportMaterial, posSimplifyPath, posSimplifySupportPath, posDetectOverhangsForLift, posSimplifyWall, posSimplifyInfill, posCount }` (`Print.hpp:93-100`).

Writer side, `PrintState::active_step_add_warning`, `PrintBase.hpp:296-321` — dedupes on `message_id` (or on `message` when `message_id == 0`) and re-marks `current`:
```cpp
auto it = (message_id == 0) ?
    std::find_if(state.warnings.begin(), state.warnings.end(), [&message](const auto &w) { return w.message_id == 0 && w.message == message; }) :
    std::find_if(state.warnings.begin(), state.warnings.end(), [message_id](const auto& w) { return w.message_id == message_id; });
if (it == state.warnings.end())
    state.warnings.emplace_back(PrintStateBase::Warning{ warning_level, true, message, message_id });
```

**`current` is the liveness flag.** `PrintState::invalidate_*` calls `mark_warnings_non_current()` on all steps (`PrintBase.hpp:283-284`), so a stale warning sticks around with `current == false`. Any reader must filter `warning.current`.

**Object identity.** The warning itself carries no object id. Identity comes from the container:
- object-level: the `PrintObject` whose `step_state_with_warnings` you read — `print_object->model_object()` (`PrintBase.hpp:337`) and `print_object->id()` (`ObjectID`).
- print-level: the `Print` itself; its id is `print.id()`.

That is exactly what the push-side event carries. `PrintBase::SlicingStatus` (`PrintBase.hpp:434-471`) has three constructors: the plain one, one taking `const PrintBase&` (sets `flags = UPDATE_PRINT_STEP_WARNINGS`, `warning_object_id = print.id()`), and one taking `const PrintObjectBase&` (sets `flags = UPDATE_PRINT_OBJECT_STEP_WARNINGS`, `warning_object_id = print_object.id()`). Fields: `warning_object_id`, `warning_step`, `message_type` (`SlicingNotificationType`, `PrintBase.hpp:59-66`), `warning_level`.

```cpp
std::optional<SliceEstimate> estimate_of(const GCodeProcessorResult& result)
{
    SliceEstimate estimate;
    const auto& statistics = result.print_statistics;
    const auto& mode = statistics.modes[static_cast<std::size_t>(PrintEstimatedStatistics::ETimeMode::Normal)];
    estimate.print_time_seconds = mode.time > 0.f ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(mode.time) : 0u;

    double cost = 0.0;
    bool   every_filament_priced = true;
    for (const auto& [extruder, volume] : statistics.total_volumes_per_extruder) {
        // A slice that used an extruder Orca has no density for cannot be
        // weighed, and a partial weight presented as the total is worse than
        // no weight at all -- so the whole estimate goes.
        if (extruder >= result.filament_densities.size()) return std::nullopt;
        const double grams = volume * result.filament_densities[extruder] * 0.001;
        estimate.material_grams += grams;
        // A filament profile with no price reports zero, which is not a price.
        if (extruder < result.filament_costs.size() && result.filament_costs[extruder] > 0.f)
            cost += grams * result.filament_costs[extruder] * 0.001;
        else
            every_filament_priced = false;
    }
    // Money is the cost of the whole print or it is not shown. With one spool
    // priced and another not, a "total" would silently leave material out.
    estimate.has_cost      = every_filament_priced && cost > 0.0;
    estimate.material_cost = estimate.has_cost ? cost : 0.0;
    // A slice that produced no material is not an estimate worth a row.
    if (estimate.print_time_seconds == 0 && estimate.material_grams <= 0.0) return std::nullopt;
    return estimate;
}
```

- **Stealth/silent time**: `modes[Stealth]` is `reset()` to 0 when the stealth estimator is off (`GCodeProcessor.cpp:6029`); `estimated_silent_print_time` is the string `"N/A"`.

Two *entirely separate* warning systems.

### System A: `PrintStateBase` step warnings (object-level and print-level)

`C:\src\JusPrin\src\libslic3r\PrintBase.hpp:54-57`:
```cpp

    NON_CRITICAL,
    CRITICAL
};
```

`PrintBase.hpp:78-98`:
```cpp
struct Warning
{
    // Critical warnings will be displayed on G-code export in a modal dialog, so that the user cannot miss them.
    WarningLevel    level;
    // If the warning is not current, then it is in an unknown state. It may or may not be valid.
    bool 			current;
    // Message to be shown to the user, UTF8, localized.
    std::string     message;
    // If message_id == 0, then the message is expected to identify the warning uniquely.
    int 			message_id;

{

    std::vector<Warning>    warnings;
```

- print-level: `PrintBaseWithState::step_state_with_warnings(PrintStepEnum step)` — `PrintBase.hpp:587`
- object-level: `PrintObjectBaseWithState::step_state_with_warnings(PrintObjectStepEnum step)` — `PrintBase.hpp:634`

```cpp

    std::find_if(state.warnings.begin(), state.warnings.end(), [&message](const auto &w) { return w.message_id == 0 && w.message == message; }) :
    std::find_if(state.warnings.begin(), state.warnings.end(), [message_id](const auto& w) { return w.message_id == message_id; });
if (it == state.warnings.end())
```

**`current` is the liveness flag.** `PrintState::invalidate_*` calls `mark_warnings_non_current()` on all steps (`PrintBase.hpp:283-284`), so a stale warning sticks around with `current == false`. Any reader must filter `warning.current`.

**Object identity.** The warning itself carries no object id. Identity comes from the container:
- object-level: the `PrintObject` whose `step_state_with_warnings` you read — `print_object->model_object()` (`PrintBase.hpp:337`) and `print_object->id()` (`ObjectID`).
- print-level: the `Print` itself; its id is `print.id()`.

That is exactly what the push-side event carries. `PrintBase::SlicingStatus` (`PrintBase.hpp:434-471`) has three constructors: the plain one, one taking `const PrintBase&` (sets `flags = UPDATE_PRINT_STEP_WARNINGS`, `warning_object_id = print.id()`), and one taking `const PrintObjectBase&` (sets `flags = UPDATE_PRINT_OBJECT_STEP_WARNINGS`, `warning_object_id = print_object.id()`).
